statement: Let $a_n=(2+\sqrt{3})^n+(2-\sqrt{3})^n$. Show that $a_n$ is an integer for every positive integer $n$ and evaluate $a_1,a_2,a_3$.
solution: Since $(2+\sqrt{3})$ and $(2-\sqrt{3})$ are conjugates, expanding both powers by the binomial theorem and adding cancels every term containing $\sqrt{3}$, so $a_n$ is an integer. Compute $a_1=4$, $a_2=(7+4\sqrt{3})+(7-4\sqrt{3})=14$, $a_3=(26+15\sqrt{3})+(26-15\sqrt{3})=52$.
hints: Expand both powers using the binomial theorem.
Add the two expansions and observe the surd terms cancel.
